newsitem.title: USA: Metals USA posts modest gains after IPO.
newsitem.headline: Metals USA posts modest gains after IPO.

text.p: Metals USA Inc, which plans to be a player consolidating the $75 billion metal processing industry, rose slightly on its first day of trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

The stock rose 5/8 to 10-5/8 on its first day, although the shares were sold for lower than the company expected when it first filed to go public. Shares were priced at $10 each, below an original price range of $12 to $14, which was cut to $11 to $12 ahead of the IPO.
Metals USA sold all the 5.9 million shares, which represent about a 28 percent equity stake. About 20.8 million shares will be outstanding after the IPO, the company said in its prospectus.
Simultaneously with the closing of the IPO, the company will buy eight companies, ("the founding companies") to form Metals USA. The group had $387 million in 1996 combined pro forma sales.
Some of the companies that will make up Metals USA include Interstate Steel Supply Co of Philadelphia, Queensboro Steel Corp of North Carolina and Texas Aluminum Industries Inc.
The lead underwriter was Alex. Brown & Sons Inc. Co-underwriters were Bear Stearns & Co Inc and Sanders Morris Mundy, according to the prospectus.

Florida Panthers Holdings Inc also made its debut on the NYSE after moving to the Big Board from the Nasdaq, where it was listed as. The company owns the Florida Panthers hockey team and several Florida resorts and hotels. Chairman Wayne Huizenga rang the opening bell to signal the start of trading at the Big Board. Shares closed down 3/8 to 22-1/2.
